main.title: Resident Evil 7: Biohazard
main.subtitle: Horror comes home
main.summary: Resident Evil 7: Biohazard is a 2017 survival horror game developed and published by Capcom.

cards.heading: Ethan Winters enters the Baker house
cards.text: Resident Evil 7: Biohazard is a 2017 survival horror game developed and published by Capcom. A main installment in the Resident Evil series, it puts the player in control of Ethan Winters as he searches for his missing wife in a derelict Louisiana plantation occupied by an infected family, solving puzzles and fighting enemies. Resident Evil 7 diverges from the more action-oriented Resident Evil 5 and Resident Evil 6, returning to the franchise's survival horror roots, emphasizing exploration. It is the first main Resident Evil game to use a first-person view.

cards.heading: The RE Engine and horror in first person
cards.text: Resident Evil 7 is the first full-length game to use Capcom's in-house RE Engine. The development was led by Koshi Nakanishi, director of Resident Evil: Revelations. A year prior to its announcement at E3 2016, it was presented as a virtual reality demo called Kitchen. The team took inspiration from the films The Texas Chain Saw Massacre (1974), The Evil Dead (1981), and Saw (2004), scaling back the game to one location, and used a first-person perspective to immerse players. Two downloadable content scenarios were released, Not a Hero and End of Zoe.

cards.heading: A return to the roots and later editions
cards.text: Resident Evil 7 was released in January 2017 for PlayStation 4, Windows, Xbox One, followed by a cloud version for the Nintendo Switch in May 2018 in Japan and December 2022 worldwide. Versions for the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S released in June 2022, with iOS, iPadOS and macOS versions following in July 2024, and a Nintendo Switch 2 version releasing in February 2026. It also supports the PlayStation VR headset. The game received generally favorable reviews and was considered a return to form for the series; critics praised Capcom's new RE Engine, gameplay, puzzles, atmosphere, and virtual reality option, but the boss battles, limited enemy variety, and the slower pace of the final chapter drew some criticism. As of June 30, 2025, the game has sold 15.4 million units, making it the 2nd best-selling game in the franchise. It was nominated for several end-of-year accolades. A sequel, Resident Evil Village, was released on May 7, 2021.

main.title: NieR:Automata
main.subtitle: Androids, machines and changing perspectives
main.summary: NieR:Automata follows android soldiers including 2B, 9S and A2 in a conflict with machine lifeforms.

cards.heading: Androids in a deserted world
cards.text: NieR:Automata follows android soldiers including 2B, 9S and A2 in a conflict with machine lifeforms. Released in 2017, it combines Yoko Taro's story with action developed by PlatinumGames. Ruined human spaces and the behaviour of their new inhabitants make the world worth examining between battles.

cards.heading: Sword attacks and Pod support
cards.text: A sword handles nearby enemies while a Pod provides ranged support. Light and heavy attacks, evasive movement and different weapons give the player ways to change pace. Character levels and equipment upgrades sit alongside those action controls, joining a role-playing structure to a game that still requires direct responses.

cards.heading: Pascal and the machines
cards.text: Pascal is a machine who rejects conflict and studies humanity. Meeting him and other machines gives 2B reasons to question the assumptions behind the war. Their behaviour and beliefs complicate the division between allied androids and enemy machines.

cards.heading: Action and character progression
cards.text: PlatinumGames combined fast combat with role-playing progression. Weapons, levels and equipment configurations accompany attacks, dodges and Pod fire. The team tuned the moments when animations could be interrupted so that weapon changes and evasive moves remained responsive.

cards.heading: Installing plug-in chips
cards.text: Plug-in chips modify an android?s statistics, combat abilities and interface. They occupy a limited amount of space, so the player must choose which advantages to install. Even HUD functions are components that can be removed. The system makes customisation part of the protagonists? mechanical bodies.

cards.heading: The story continues after the first ending
cards.text: Completing the first ending opens further routes through the story. Later play changes the character and reveals information missing from earlier scenes. As 9S, hacking and new dialogue alter encounters first experienced through 2B. Returning to familiar places gradually reveals a larger conflict.

cards.heading: Encounters beyond the main mission
cards.text: Side quests lead through ruined cities, deserts, forests and industrial sites. Assignments from Resistance members and machines introduce smaller stories of work, fear, memory and imitation. These encounters develop the inhabitants beyond their roles in the main conflict.

cards.heading: Keiichi Okabe?s changing score
cards.text: Keiichi Okabe sought a more dynamic sound than in the first NieR while retaining its voices and melancholy. Battle music could begin from a beat, while other pieces began with a melody imagined as a voice. The score follows shifts between exploration and fighting while giving revisited places recognisable themes.

cards.heading: Tuning the transitions between movements
cards.text: PlatinumGames used test levels to check animations and effects. Takahisa Taura described tools for controlling precisely when one movement could be cancelled into the next. That work let players link attacks, dodges and weapon changes without waiting for every animation to finish.

main.title: Hollow Knight
main.subtitle: Beneath the surface, a kingdom to listen to
main.summary: Hollow Knight is a 2017 Metroidvania video game developed and published by Australian independent development studio Team Cherry.

cards.heading: Exploring the fallen kingdom of Hallownest
cards.text: Hollow Knight is a 2017 Metroidvania video game developed and published by Australian independent development studio Team Cherry. The player controls a nameless insectoid warrior (commonly known as "The Knight") in exploring Hallownest, a fallen kingdom plagued by a supernatural disease. The game is set in diverse subterranean locations, featuring friendly and hostile insectoid characters and numerous bosses. Players have the opportunity to unlock abilities as they explore, along with pieces of lore and flavour text that are spread throughout the kingdom.

cards.heading: From a game jam to a crowdfunded world
cards.text: The concept behind Hollow Knight was conceived in 2013 in the Ludum Dare game jam. Adelaide-based Team Cherry—founded by artist Ari Gibson and web designer William Pellen—wanted to create a game inspired by older platformers that replicated the explorational aspects of its influences. Inspirations for the game include Faxanadu, Metroid, Zelda II: The Adventure of Link, and Mega Man X. Development was partially funded through a crowdfunding campaign that raised over A$57,000 by the end of 2014. It was released for Linux, macOS, and Windows in early 2017, for the Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One in 2018, and for the Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S in 2026. Between 2017 and 2018, four free downloadable expansions were released.

cards.heading: An audience grows around the underground
cards.text: Hollow Knight was well-received by critics, with particular praise for its music, art style, worldbuilding, atmosphere, combat, and level of difficulty. It has since been regarded by some critics as one of the greatest games of all time. The game has sold more than 15 million copies. A sequel following major character Hornet, Hollow Knight: Silksong, was released in September of 2025 to commercial success and critical acclaim.

cards.heading: A map that asks for attention
cards.text: Cornifer sells a first outline of each area. With the quill, the Knight adds discoveries to the map when resting. Between benches, the player relies on landmarks and memory to retrace a route or find a way into unfamiliar tunnels.

cards.heading: Defeat, the Shade and lost Geo
cards.text: The player has a limited number of hit points, which are represented by masks. By striking enemies, the player character gains Soul, which is stored in a "Soul Vessel". Initially, the player can only use Soul to "Focus" which regenerates masks, but as the game progresses, players unlock and collect several offensive spells, which consume Soul. Soul can also be used for some charms which are in-game boosters that help The Knight. If all masks are lost, the player dies, and a Shade appears at the approximate location of the player's death, marked on the map. The player loses all Geo, the game's main currency, and can only hold a reduced amount of Soul; they must defeat the Shade to recover lost Geo and regain their lost Soul capacity. If the player dies before the Shade is defeated, a new Shade appears, erasing the previous one alongside the Geo it was holding.

main.title: Horizon Zero Dawn
main.subtitle: Reading machines, uncovering the past
main.summary: Horizon Zero Dawn introduced Aloy, an outcast trying to understand her own past in a world inhabited by animal-like machines.

cards.heading: A hunter among machines
cards.text: Horizon Zero Dawn introduced Aloy, an outcast trying to understand her own past in a world inhabited by animal-like machines. Guerrilla's 2017 action role-playing game set tribal settlements beside the remains of a much older technological civilisation. The two histories are connected, although their relationship is initially unclear.

cards.heading: Look before drawing the bow
cards.text: Aloy's Focus helps her examine machines, and her weapons let her approach encounters with different preparations. Learning what a machine carries and how it moves can matter more than repeatedly striking its largest surface. Hunting becomes a sequence of observation, a chosen tool and a response to what changes.

cards.heading: The ruins can speak
cards.text: The Focus can also recover recordings from ancient ruins. These fragments connect a place the player explores with people who once used it. The same device that helps Aloy read an immediate threat therefore helps her investigate the larger question of what happened to the world.

main.title: Fast RMX
main.subtitle: A launch-day race above the ground
main.summary: Fast RMX is Shin'en Multimedia's futuristic racing game, released alongside Nintendo Switch on 3 March 2017.

cards.heading: A launch-day race above the ground
cards.text: Fast RMX is Shin'en Multimedia's futuristic racing game, released alongside Nintendo Switch on 3 March 2017. Anti-gravity vehicles race through industrial structures, deserts and other high-speed circuits. It expands Fast Racing Neo with new courses while adapting the series to the Switch's portable and docked forms. The defining action is changing the vehicle's phase between two colours, matching boost strips and jump pads as the track rushes towards the player and an approaching corner competes for attention.

cards.heading: Change colour at the right moment
cards.text: A matching phase lets the vehicle benefit from a coloured section of track. Reading that colour, switching in time and maintaining a useful racing line become parts of the same movement. Energy collected around the course supplies additional boosts, giving the player some control over where to accelerate beyond the fixed strips. Grand Prix events group races into cups, rewarding consistent placement rather than a single successful lap. Faster classes make previously manageable routes demand earlier decisions and more precise reactions.

cards.heading: Spend speed carefully in Hero Mode
cards.text: The original release offered thirty courses, with a later free update increasing the total to thirty-six. Local split-screen supports four players, and online races allow up to eight. Hero Mode changes the risk by making boost energy serve as the machine's health as well, so spending everything for speed can leave little margin for a collision. Fast RMX concentrates its identity in that continuing balance between reading the next coloured section and deciding how much acceleration the current situation can safely afford.

main.title: Snipperclips: Cut It Out, Together!
main.subtitle: Two paper bodies become the tools
main.summary: Snipperclips: Cut It Out, Together! is SFB Games' cooperative puzzle game, released alongside Switch on 3 March 2017.

cards.heading: Two paper bodies become the tools
cards.text: Snipperclips: Cut It Out, Together! is SFB Games' cooperative puzzle game, released alongside Switch on 3 March 2017. Snip and Clip are paper-like characters whose overlapping bodies can be cut into new shapes. The player uses those changing outlines to solve small physical problems, from fitting a template to carrying an object or popping a balloon. The characters themselves become the equipment, making a puzzle's solution something the players create together rather than an item they simply find in the room.

cards.heading: Cut a shape that solves the problem
cards.text: Rotating and overlapping the two figures determines the shape removed by a snip. A useful hook, cup or sharp point can emerge from the same starting bodies, and the pair must position themselves carefully to produce it. The result also needs to work in motion: a shape that looks promising may handle an object awkwardly once it is carried. The puzzle therefore continues through communication and experimentation, with each attempt showing the players more about the relationship between the outline they made and the task ahead.

cards.heading: An idea made for sharing a Joy-Con
cards.text: The project began as Adam and Tom Vian's Flash prototype Friendshapes before Nintendo helped develop it into a Switch release. The art-supply setting and expressive faces keep failed attempts playful. World mode supports one or two players, while Party and Blitz introduce cooperative and competitive activities for up to four. Calum Bowen composed the music. Sharing the console's controllers suits the idea especially well, placing two people beside one screen where the next cut can be proposed, tested and laughed over immediately. The expanded Snipperclips Plus edition followed on 10 November 2017.
